module_intro: Subtopics: PD-Array Framework & Hierarchy, FVG / OB / Breaker / Mitigation / IFVG, Confluence, Failure & Repricing.
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Advanced Modules 1--4. PD arrays are no longer isolated entry tools; they are the specific price levels at which the delivery narrative (liquidity + structure + range) is expected to react, continue or fail.
module_objectives: Locate every relevant PD array inside the controlling dealing range and grade it by hierarchy and location (premium/discount).
Distinguish Order Block, Breaker, Mitigation Block and Inversion FVG by formation and polarity behaviour.
Apply Consequent Encroachment as a refinement inside an FVG.
Recognise PD-array confluence and PD-array failure and state the narrative implication of each.
Select the highest-probability array for entry given the current delivery leg, Draw on Liquidity and structural confirmation.
Classify less-supported constructs (e.g. Rejection Block) appropriately and avoid elevating them above primary ICT arrays.
Integrate PD-array choice into the multi-timeframe delivery narrative rather than treating arrays as standalone signals.
Higher-timeframe unmitigated structural levels and unmitigated higher-timeframe Order Blocks / FVGs that align with the delivery narrative.
Unmitigated Order Blocks that originated the most recent displacement + MSS.
Fair Value Gaps created by that same displacement (especially at Consequent Encroachment).
Breaker Blocks that meet quality filters (prior high-quality OB, clear violation, displacement in the new direction).
Mitigation / partially mitigated arrays that still show reaction potential.
Lower-timeframe or heavily mitigated arrays.
State the controlling dealing range and whether price is in premium or discount relative to the intended direction.
State the Draw on Liquidity and the structural confirmation status.
List the unmitigated PD arrays that sit in the correct half of the range and that were created by (or align with) the current delivery displacement.
Rank them by the practical hierarchy and by confluence.
Select the highest-ranked array that still offers acceptable invalidation distance.
Require lower-timeframe conditioning (liquidity raid + displacement + MSS) before entry if the narrative demands it.
If no array satisfies location, hierarchy and narrative alignment, stand aside.

concepts.name: PD Array Framework - Advanced Premise
concepts.definition: A PD Array (Premium / Discount Array) is any ICT price reference that the algorithm is expected to respect or reprice when price returns to it, conditioned by its location in premium or discount relative to the controlling dealing range. Arrays are not zones of magic; they are the recorded footprints of prior institutional activity and imbalance.

raw_sections.Role in Delivery:
Within the delivery sequence (Module 1), PD arrays form during displacement and become the retracement objectives during the retracement / rebalancing phase. They are the precise locations at which the trader may enter in the direction of the Draw on Liquidity after structural confirmation (Module 4).

**Evidence Classification:** *A - PD Array terminology and the premium/discount conditioning of arrays are core ICT.*

concepts.name: Core PD Arrays
concepts.definition: A three-candle imbalance in which the wick of the first and third candles do not fully overlap, leaving a gap in price delivery. Bullish FVG is sometimes labelled BISI (Buy-side Imbalance, Sell-side Inefficiency); bearish FVG is sometimes labelled SIBI. The FVG is both a record of displacement and a potential retracement magnet.

raw_sections.Fair Value Gap (FVG) / Imbalance: A three-candle imbalance in which the wick of the first and third candles do not fully overlap, leaving a gap in price delivery. Bullish FVG is sometimes labelled BISI (Buy-side Imbalance, Sell-side Inefficiency); bearish FVG is sometimes labelled SIBI. The FVG is both a record of displacement and a potential retracement magnet.
raw_sections.Order Block (OB): The last opposing candle (or small cluster) before a displacement that breaks structure. It is the presumed origin of the institutional order flow that produced the energetic move. High-quality OBs are those that form after a liquidity event and are followed by genuine displacement and MSS.
raw_sections.Breaker Block: A previously valid Order Block that has been violated by a body close beyond its far boundary, after which the zone is expected to act with inverted polarity. A failed bullish OB becomes a bearish Breaker (resistance on the return); a failed bearish OB becomes a bullish Breaker.
raw_sections.Mitigation Block: An Order Block that is retested without a decisive body close beyond its far boundary, and from which price continues in the original direction. The return is understood as residual interest being satisfied before continuation. (Note: community definitions of Mitigation vs Breaker vary; the body-close test remains the clearest operational delimiter.)
raw_sections.Inversion Fair Value Gap (IFVG):
A Fair Value Gap that has been traded through and that subsequently acts with inverted polarity. The former bullish FVG, once mitigated and closed through, may act as resistance on the return, and vice versa.

**Evidence Classification:** *A/B - FVG, Order Block, Breaker and Mitigation are primary ICT. BISI/SIBI and IFVG appear in ICT teaching and later refinements. Exact Mitigation vs Breaker boundary shows some variation across presentations.*

concepts.name: Consequent Encroachment
concepts.definition:
Consequent Encroachment (CE) is the midpoint (50 %) of a Fair Value Gap. ICT often treats the CE as a refined entry or reaction reference inside the larger FVG. Advanced practice uses CE when the full FVG is wide and a tighter invalidation or more precise entry is desired, while still respecting the higher-timeframe narrative.

**Evidence Classification:** *A - Consequent Encroachment is explicit ICT terminology.*

concepts.name: Liquidity Void and Balanced Price Range
concepts.definition: An area of rapid price movement with little to no trading activity - the extreme expression of imbalance. Closely related to FVG; some presentations treat voids as the more extreme form. Price may return to rebalance the void as part of the delivery narrative.

raw_sections.Balanced Price Range:
A range in which opposing imbalances have been filled or in which price has spent sufficient time to leave the area relatively efficient. Balanced ranges are less attractive as immediate retracement magnets than fresh, unmitigated imbalances.

**Evidence Classification:** *B/C - Liquidity void and balanced price range language appears in ICT material in connection with imbalance and efficiency; precise boundaries with FVG terminology are sometimes fluid.*

concepts.name: Rejection Block - Classification Note
concepts.definition:
Rejection Block (a wick-based rejection zone after a liquidity sweep) appears frequently in community PD-array matrices and secondary materials. Primary ICT teaching emphasises Order Blocks, FVGs, Breakers and related constructs more consistently than a distinct "Rejection Block" category. Advanced students may observe wick rejections as price action, but should not elevate Rejection Block above the primary arrays without explicit primary support for the specific trade.

**Evidence Classification:** *D - Community terminology / secondary emphasis. Use with caution; do not treat as equal to core ICT arrays.*

concepts.name: PD-Array Hierarchy (Practical Advanced Ranking)
concepts.definition:
When multiple arrays compete inside the same region of the controlling range, a practical hierarchy (strongest to weaker, all else equal) is:

- Higher-timeframe unmitigated structural levels and unmitigated higher-timeframe Order Blocks / FVGs that align with the delivery narrative.

- Unmitigated Order Blocks that originated the most recent displacement + MSS.

- Fair Value Gaps created by that same displacement (especially at Consequent Encroachment).

- Breaker Blocks that meet quality filters (prior high-quality OB, clear violation, displacement in the new direction).

- Mitigation / partially mitigated arrays that still show reaction potential.

- Lower-timeframe or heavily mitigated arrays.

Hierarchy is always subordinate to: (1) alignment with the Draw on Liquidity, (2) location in the correct premium/discount half of the controlling range, and (3) structural confirmation.

**Evidence Classification:** *C - Practical synthesis. ICT presents the family of arrays; exact numerical rankings are community refinements of that family.*

concepts.name: PD-Array Confluence
concepts.definition: Confluence exists when two or more arrays overlap or sit immediately adjacent (e.g., Order Block overlapping an FVG, or CE of an FVG sitting inside a higher-timeframe OB). Confluence raises the quality of the location provided the higher-timeframe narrative and range filter are satisfied. Confluence does not override a conflicting Draw on Liquidity or a wrong-half location.

concepts.name: PD-Array Failure
concepts.definition: An array fails when price trades through it with decisive displacement and closes beyond its far boundary in a manner that negates its expected polarity. Failure of an Order Block produces a Breaker candidate. Failure of an FVG may produce an IFVG candidate. Failure of the array that was expected to hold the delivery leg challenges the current narrative.

concepts.definition:
- State the controlling dealing range and whether price is in premium or discount relative to the intended direction.

- State the Draw on Liquidity and the structural confirmation status.

- List the unmitigated PD arrays that sit in the correct half of the range and that were created by (or align with) the current delivery displacement.

- Rank them by the practical hierarchy and by confluence.

- Select the highest-ranked array that still offers acceptable invalidation distance.

- Require lower-timeframe conditioning (liquidity raid + displacement + MSS) before entry if the narrative demands it.

- If no array satisfies location, hierarchy and narrative alignment, stand aside.

worked_narrative_examples.name: Worked Narrative - PD Array Inside Delivery
worked_narrative_examples.definition:
Weekly DOL: buy-side above 1.1200. Weekly and daily ranges in discount. Daily SSL swept; daily bullish displacement and MSS printed; daily bullish FVG and Order Block overlap at 1.0630 - 1.0660 (discount of both ranges).

London: further sell-side raid; 15-minute bullish MSS; 15-minute FVG forms inside the daily array.

Selection: The daily OB/FVG confluence in discount is the primary array. The 15-minute FVG is the refinement. Entry on retracement into the 15-minute FVG / CE, invalidation below the daily displacement origin. Target hierarchy: daily internal buy-side, then weekly ERL.

This is PD-array selection fully subordinated to delivery, range and structure.

common_misinterpretations.name: Common Misinterpretations
common_misinterpretations.definition:
1096. Trading every FVG or Order Block regardless of premium/discount location and higher-timeframe DOL.

1097. Treating Breaker and Mitigation as interchangeable.

1098. Elevating Rejection Block or other community labels above core ICT arrays.

1099. Ignoring array failure and continuing to treat a violated zone as supportive in its original polarity.

1100. Selecting a lower-timeframe array that conflicts with the controlling range's location filter.

1101. Using PD arrays as standalone signals without a delivery narrative.

evidence_summary.name: Evidence Summary
evidence_summary.definition:
Fair Value Gap, Order Block, Breaker, Mitigation, Consequent Encroachment and the PD-array framing are primary ICT. BISI/SIBI and IFVG appear in ICT teaching. Liquidity void and balanced price range are used in connection with imbalance. Rejection Block is primarily community/secondary. Practical hierarchy rankings are synthesis; ICT supplies the family of arrays and the premium/discount conditioning, not a rigid numerical scorecard.

***Source / Research note:** Primary orientation: ICT teaching on Order Blocks, Fair Value Gaps, Breakers, Mitigation, Consequent Encroachment and PD arrays in premium/discount. Secondary matrices and rankings used only as practical synthesis and clearly labelled.*

key_terms: PD Array - any ICT price reference conditioned by premium/discount location inside the dealing range.
Fair Value Gap (FVG) / BISI / SIBI - three-candle imbalance left by displacement.
Order Block - last opposing candle before displacement.
Breaker - violated Order Block with inverted polarity.
Mitigation Block - retested OB that holds and continues original direction.
IFVG - Fair Value Gap that has inverted polarity after being traded through.
Consequent Encroachment - midpoint of an FVG; refined reaction reference.
PD-array confluence - overlap or adjacency of two or more arrays.
PD-array failure - decisive trade-through that negates expected polarity.
